definition: A Tsetlin machine is an artificial intelligence algorithm based on propositional logic.
details: A Tsetlin machine is an artificial intelligence algorithm based on propositional logic.

explainer.lead: A Tsetlin machine is an AI algorithm built on propositional logic rather than arithmetic weights. It matters as a learning approach whose decisions take the form of logical clauses.

tiers.eli5: Instead of scoring things with numbers, it learns rules like 'if A and B, then yes' and votes with them.
tiers.practitioner: It is attractive where interpretable, clause-based decisions and hardware-friendly computation are wanted. A pitfall is that clause structure can be harder to scale and tune than conventional neural networks.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, it learns a set of conjunctive clauses over binary inputs, combined by votes to produce output; clauses are updated by team-based automata. Its limits are mainly around representation of continuous inputs and scaling.

explainer.example: Given binary features describing a customer, learned clauses such as 'if high balance and late payment then default' vote on the outcome.
